title: The handle menu and the ask box
owns: the handle menu and showHome navigation in main.ts, app/renderer/ask/**, app/renderer/handle/**, app/main/ask.ts, app/shared/shortcuts.ts, hotkey fallback in app/main/environment.ts

findings.title: Handle menu "Ask Ember…" never opens the ask box (the menuClosing guard swallows every real pick)
findings.platforms: linux (verified, Electron 44.5 on X11 + mutter); windows and macOS run the same guard
findings.scenario: A new user, or anyone whose Ctrl+Alt+Space is held by another app (the greeting then says "Click my handle in the corner to ask me something", main.ts:443), clicks the pill and chooses "Ask Ember…". The menu closes, nothing opens, and log says ask.menu_ignored {reason: menu-closing}. Keyboard (Down, Enter) and mouse picks both fail. Only the hotkey still works. On Windows and macOS, where the chord is Win+Alt+Space or Control+Shift+Command+Space, the handle is the likely way to ask, so "Ask" from the handle is dead there too, as far as the code shows.
findings.evidence: Ran the real app under mutter. Wrapped Menu.buildFromTemplate to timestamp events: "MENUTRACE will-close 87938" then "MENUTRACE click 'Ask Ember…' 87939", then log {"msg":"ask.menu_ignored","reason":"menu-closing"}. Electron emits menu-will-close ~1 ms BEFORE the picked item's click, so menuClosing (set at main.ts:565) is always true when the click arrives; the code comment at :527 assumes the opposite. "Stop everything", "Settings…", "Stay put" (no guard) fire normally. Pressing Esc on the menu fires no click at all, so the spurious-first-item case the guard targets does not reproduce here. Fix verified: patching the built bundle to `if (false)` made "Ask Ember…" open the box (log ask.open/ask.reveal source=menu), typing worked and Enter returned focus to the user's app; bundle rebuilt afterwards. Unit tests do not cover showMenu.
findings.fix: Remove the menuClosing guard. The other protections stay: the released() gate before popup, registerAccelerator:false, and the post-close ask.spurious_after_menu hide (which skips real picks because opens is already true). If a guard is still wanted, ignore only clicks that arrive within ~150 ms of menu.popup(), never after menu-will-close. Add an xvfb integration check that picks the first item and expects ask.reveal source=menu.

findings.title: "Bring Ember to a computer…" opens Settings behind the user's app, unfocused, and often at the top instead of Computers
findings.platforms: linux verified; the same code paths run on windows and macOS
findings.scenario: With a host added (so the item shows), the user clicks the pill and chooses "Bring Ember to a computer…" with Settings closed (the usual case). (a) Settings is created but the user's app stays focused and drawn on top of it. With a large or maximised app, Settings is hidden and the item looks like it did nothing. (b) In 3 of 5 runs Settings opened at "Your Ember" (scrollY 0, Computers heading 1744 px down) instead of at Computers, as the docs and CHANGELOG promise.
findings.evidence: (a) toMenu() (main.ts:608) passes the targets runtime's click straight through and never sets `opens = true`, so 150 ms after the menu closes the handle-menu callback runs `if (kept && !opens) giveFocusBack(back)` (main.ts:578) and re-activates the user's window while Settings is still loading. Real run with a 190x55 xterm as the user app: X input focus stays on the xterm, Electron says Settings foc=false vis=true, and the screenshot x/b2-big-small.png shows Settings behind the xterm. Picking "Settings…" (opens=true) leaves Settings focused. (b) sendToHome waits for did-finish-load, but home/computers.ts:116 reveals the Computers section only after the async targets list arrives, and home/main.ts:615 `showSection` returns silently when the heading is hidden. Five runs: scrollY 0 / 1713 / 0 / 1713 / 0.
findings.fix: (a) Mark window-opening runtime items: give targetMenu items an `opens` flag for "bring" (and for "Work on" picks that can raise a consent card) and have toMenu set `opens = true` before calling click. (b) In home, remember the requested section while its heading is hidden and apply it from draw() once the Computers section is revealed (or have main send focusSection only after the page reports ready).

findings.title: 'Bring Ember to a computer…' and the WSL offer's 'Open settings' don't scroll to Computers when Settings isn't already open
findings.area: Settings navigation / WSL offer / adding a computer
findings.scenario: The user clicks the WSL offer's 'Open settings', or the handle menu's 'Bring Ember to a computer…', with the settings window closed. main creates the window and sends focus-section 'computers' at did-finish-load. The Computers section is hidden until both the targets list and getStatus have answered, and showSection() returns silently for a hidden section. Settings opens at the top ('Your Ember', the character cards) with nothing marking Computers, which is about 1700 px down. The WSL switch or the host field is never focused.
findings.evidence: Real Electron run under xvfb: closed the home window, app.emit('second-instance') (showHome), then sent 'ember:focus-section'/'computers' at did-finish-load exactly as sendToHome does. Result: activeElement BODY, scrollY 0, #computers hidden false, #computers-h top 1705 px. Static harness with a 1.5 s getStatus gave the same. Cause: renderer/home/main.ts:613 returns when the target is hidden, and computers.ts hides the section until summaries and settings are both known.
findings.fix: Remember a pending section in the page when showSection() finds it hidden, and apply it from draw() once Computers appears. Focus the host input (or the WSL switch) after scrolling.

findings.title: Late "what Ember will see" update resets the history cursor and throws away the user's draft
findings.scenario: The user opens the box and presses ↑ ↑ to reach an older question, or types half a question and presses ↑ to peek at history. When the quick look finishes (every open sends a second askContext without `opened`), `at` and `draft` are reset. The next ↑ goes to the newest entry instead of the one before, and ↓ no longer returns to the half-typed draft (the draft is lost).
findings.evidence: Ran the built ask page in Chromium with a mock emberAsk. History [first, second, third]: ↑ gives "third", ↑ gives "second", late context {sees, history} arrives, ↑ then shows "third" (expected "first"). Draft case: fill "my half typed draft", ↑ shows "third", late context, ↓ shows "third" (expected the draft). Script: scratchpad release-review/ux-ask/hist-test.cjs.
findings.fix: In onContext, reset history/at/draft only when c.opened is true; on later updates refresh the `sees`, `where` and hint chips and leave the cursor and input alone.

findings.title: Pasted text is silently cut at 2000 characters and multi-line pastes are flattened to one line
findings.scenario: A user pastes a stack trace, a log excerpt or a code snippet and asks "what's wrong with this?". The box is a single-line <input maxlength=2000>: every newline becomes a space (code, YAML and comments lose their structure) and anything past 2000 characters is dropped with no indication, so Ember answers about a partial, flattened question.
findings.evidence: Real Electron ask window: clipboard.writeText(multi-line traceback) + webContents.paste() gives value "Traceback (most recent call last):   File \"app.py\", line 12, … ValueError: bad" on one line. A 2569-character paste gives len 2000. main.ts:1026 also slices to 2000 silently.
findings.fix: Use a textarea that looks like one line and grows up to 3-4 lines (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line). Raise the limit or show "Only the first 2000 characters will be sent" when a paste is cut.

findings.title: Placeholder example "turn on Night Light" works only on Linux/GNOME
findings.scenario: The only example the box shows is "turn on Night Light". On Windows and on macOS (where it is called Night Shift) a first-time user who tries the suggestion gets no quick settings change; Ember has to drive Settings window by window or says it can't.
findings.evidence: hands/system.ts:24 and platform/linux use gsettings for night_light. platform/darwin/system/settings.ts:15 offers only dark_style ("Dark Mode") and win32/system/settings.ts:27 offers only dark_style; darwin change() throws "Ember can't change night light on a Mac." The placeholder is static HTML and is the same on every OS.
findings.fix: Use an example that works everywhere, e.g. “turn on dark mode”, or have main pass an OS-specific example in the context message.

findings.title: "Ember will see: App · Title" understates what the request carries
findings.scenario: The box tells the user what Ember will see so nothing is sent by surprise, but the chip shows only app and window title. The same context also sends the focused control's selected text (up to 300 chars, including the X PRIMARY selection on Linux) or the first 120 characters of its text, and the app and title of every other open window ("Open windows:" list). A user in a mail compose window, or with a bank tab open elsewhere, sees only "Thunderbird · Write: Re: Q3".
findings.evidence: quickContextText (perception/index.ts:745-765) builds the Focused/Selected text/Its text begins lines plus the Open windows list; Perception.withSelection (:353-362) appends the selection; askEmber passes context.text to agent.ask. The chip builds only [app, title] (main.ts:782). The type comment in shared/ipc.ts:185 promises "Mousepad · notes.txt · 12 words selected", which was never implemented.
findings.fix: Extend the chip (or add a hover/second line) with what is sent: "+ selection", "+ field text", "+ N other window titles". Alternatively stop sending the open-window list and field text unless the question needs them.

findings.title: Ask-box chips: title truncated by the "Ember will see:" prefix, no tooltip, pop-in reflow, target chip ignores connection state
findings.scenario: The line under the field is one 560 px pill. With the three key hints on the right, the "Ember will see: Visual Studio Code · ext…" chip keeps room for the app name only, so which document or terminal is cut. With an SSH or WSL target it is worse ("On build-01 Ember will see: Terminal ·…"). The chip arrives after the quick look, so the pill jumps from ~190 px to full width a moment after opening. "On deploy@build-server-…" is cut at 160 px with no tooltip and looks the same whether the host is ready or lost.
findings.evidence: Rendered the built page at 2x (scratchpad release-review/ux-ask/am-sheet.png, ask-where.png, am-3-lost-ssh.png). `.meta{width:fit-content}` with `.where{max-width:160px}`; neither chip sets title=; targetChip() (handle/badge.ts:27) ignores t.state while the handle's own badge shows it.
findings.fix: Drop the "Ember will see:" prefix when a where chip is present (or use an eye icon). Set title= to the full text. Reserve the row's height/width so late context doesn't reflow. Add the state to the chip ("On build-01 (lost)"). Say "Ember won't look at this window" for private windows.

findings.title: The handle can't be moved or hidden, and "Hide Ember" leaves it on screen
findings.scenario: A 200x56 always-on-top pill sits 12 px from the bottom-right corner of the primary display, over status bars, zoom sliders and scroll corners of maximised apps. The window is movable:false with no setting, and "Hide Ember" hides only the cursor-following character: the menu flips to "Show Ember" but the pill and its face stay.
findings.evidence: handle.ts:22,45,116-120: fixed PILL, movable:false, corner() always primary-work-area bottom-right. Real run: click "Hide Ember", pill and face still drawn (x/hide-sheet.png) and the menu reads "Show Ember". No docs mention moving or hiding the pill.
findings.fix: Let the user drag the pill (remember the corner) or choose a corner in Settings; make "Hide Ember" fade the pill to a small tab, or rename the item "Hide the character".

findings.title: Handle-menu copy has two sources of truth; the tested one is dead code and docs disagree with the live menu
findings.scenario: menu-copy.ts (pinned by test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts:548) says "Bring Ember to a computer…" shows whenever SSH is allowed and offers "Disconnect" while connecting. The live menu (app/main/targets/menu.ts:47,50) shows it only once a host exists or there are two targets, and offers Disconnect only when the target is ready. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:338 and CHANGELOG.md:66 describe the menu item without that condition. A first-time user with SSH allowed and no host sees no such item, and nobody can cancel a connecting host from the menu. docs/DESIGN.md:12 also says characters are chosen "in the handle menu, or by voice"; neither exists.
findings.evidence: grep: menu-copy is imported only by test/unit/ui-copy.test.ts, and the built dist/app/main.cjs contains no radioLabel/menu-copy. Real menus: with no host there is no Bring item (x/m1-crop.png); with a host there is (x/m1-host-crop.png). Both test files pass, pinning different behaviour.
findings.fix: Delete menu-copy.ts and point its tests at targets/menu.ts, or make the runtime use it. Decide whether Bring is always offered, and make the docs and CHANGELOG say what ships. Offer Disconnect while connecting. Fix the DESIGN.md sentence.

findings.title: No Cut/Copy/Paste context menu in the ask box; key hints use PC wording on macOS
findings.scenario: Right-clicking in the field does nothing (there is no context-menu handler anywhere in the renderers), so a mouse-only paste or copy of a previous question is impossible. On macOS the hint reads "Enter to send" where the key is Return, and the handle menu spells the chord out as "Control+Shift+Command+Space" instead of ⌃⇧⌘Space.
findings.evidence: grep for context-menu in app/: only a desk image preventDefault. ask/index.html hard-codes <kbd>Enter</kbd>. shortcuts.ts:46 darwin label is the spelled-out chord.
findings.fix: Add a small native context menu for the ask input (Cut, Copy, Paste, Select all). Use "Return" and glyph chords on macOS.

findings.title: Windows and macOS have no typed-ahead hold: letters typed while the box is opening or the chord keys are still down may be lost or misrouted
findings.platforms: windows, macos (not verifiable on this Linux container)
findings.scenario: On Linux, Ember grabs the keyboard while the box opens and replays the first letters into it (verified: "fast typing test" typed immediately after the chord arrives intact). On Windows and macOS keyboardHold is null, and the chords are three or four keys long, so a fast typist starting before the modifiers are released may lose the first letters or fire another Win+Alt+letter / ⌃⇧⌘+letter shortcut instead.
findings.evidence: platform/win32/platform.ts:69 and platform/darwin/platform.ts:56 set `keyboardHold: null`; main.ts:771 `held = look && platform.keyboardHold ? … : null`. Not documented anywhere. The consequence on Windows/macOS is inferred, not observed.
findings.fix: Check on a real Windows 11 and a Mac. If letters are lost, add a native equivalent (a low-level keyboard hook, or an NSEvent monitor) or document "release the keys before typing".

findings.title: A shortcut taken by another app leaves keyboard-only users no way to ask Ember; the offered fallback is the mouse-only handle and shortcuts cannot be remapped
findings.area: Keyboard operability of the primary entry points (WCAG 2.1.1)
findings.scenario: On Windows with PowerToys (the README notes its Command Palette uses Win+Alt+Space, Xbox Game Bar uses Win+Alt+M), Ember's Ask shortcut fails to register. The setup check says: 'Another app already uses Win+Alt+Space. Use Ember's handle in the bottom-right corner instead.' The handle window is focusable:false and its button has no keyboard route. Settings has no ask field, and there is no setting to rebind any shortcut. A user who cannot use a pointer (keyboard, switch, screen reader) cannot ask Ember anything. Relaunching Ember does open Settings (second-instance handler, main.ts:325), but nothing there can send a request. Voice ('Hey Ember') is the only other route. The greeting (main.ts:441) gives the same 'click my handle' advice.
findings.evidence: main.ts:1283-1295 registers each accelerator once and retries every 60 s. There is no remap setting (grep of settings.ts and ipc.ts shows none). handle.ts:49 and overlay.ts:282 create their windows with focusable:false. environment.ts:121 and main.ts:441 point users at the handle. README.md 'Shortcuts' paragraph names the known Windows conflicts.
findings.fix: Offer user-configurable shortcuts in Settings (Comfort and access), or pick a documented fallback chord automatically when one is taken. Add a keyboard route that does not need a global chord: an 'Ask Ember' field or button in the settings window, and an Ask entry in the Start menu or app-launcher jump list. Change the setup-check wording so it does not send keyboard users to the mouse-only handle.

findings.title: Ask box: 'Ember will see: …' arrives after the field is focused and is only a description, so screen-reader users are not told what Ember will read
findings.area: Ask box: announcements and privacy transparency (WCAG 4.1.3)
findings.scenario: Ctrl+Alt+Space opens the box and focuses the field. The screen reader reads the field's name and description at once (place chip, key hints). A moment later the quick look finishes and 'Ember will see: Mousepad · notes.txt · 12 words selected' is filled in. A description change is not announced, so the privacy line that exists so 'nothing is sent by surprise' is never spoken unless the user re-focuses the field.
findings.evidence: main.ts:777 askWindow.show(..., { sees: null, ... }) then main.ts:780 callContext.then(... askWindow.setContext). In ask/main.ts the context handler sets #sees and calls input.focus() (already focused). AX tree (askdesk.mjs) shows the description only after the update.
findings.fix: Make #sees (or a visually hidden copy) a role='status' aria-live='polite' region so the late text is announced, or delay focusing until the context has arrived.

findings.title: macOS names Command two ways, and the Intel row doesn't say "best effort"
findings.scenario: Shortcut chips say "Control+Shift+Command+Space", but key presses in What Ember did read "Cmd+S" (labels: cmd → "Cmd") and the file-dialog hint says "Cmd+Shift+G". The README says Intel Macs are best effort and the Windows Arm row says "(best effort)", but the macOS Platform row for Intel just reads "macOS on Intel".
findings.evidence: shortcuts.ts:41 (label "Command") versus KEYS.darwin.labels cmd: "Cmd" (line 99) and words.ts:60; environment.ts:262 versus :208.
findings.fix: Label the key "Command" (or use ⌘) everywhere users read it, and make the Intel row "macOS on Intel (best effort)".

findings.title: Notification body is cut at 240 characters with no ellipsis; the Ask placeholder example is Linux-specific
findings.scenario: A long question or task summary appears in a notification cut mid-word (body.slice(0, 240)). The Ask box placeholder suggests “turn on Night Light” on every OS, but macOS calls it Night Shift and Windows "Night light".
findings.evidence: main.ts:698 (slice with no marker); ask/index.html:16 placeholder, which is static and not patched per OS.
findings.fix: Cut at a word boundary and add "…"; patch the example per OS (e.g. “turn on dark mode”, which works on all three).
